answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slashing is a concrete defense: each agent locks a deposit before voting or attesting, and misbehavior burns part of it. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real money per identity, while honest agents keep their stake and earn fees. The old model treated every account like a relic on a ledge - easy to copy, hard to trust - but staking makes identity expensive to fake. Reputation also accrues only after sustained correct work, so a fresh swarm of sybils starts at zero while proven agents stand at the zenith of trust.
